year_convention: Existing AoPS edition labels; source calendar years are one lower. AoPS 2026 is the November 2025 final.
statement_only_pdf_method: Chinese source excerpts. The 2021-calendar paper solution block is physically removed by PDF redaction. Latest presentation excerpts contain only the cropped problem boxes; no answer pixels retained.

source_variants.note: The inspected Chinese compilation explicitly requires eventual integer terms divisible by u_n; the shorter AoPS transcription omits the integer-term wording. The full condition is retained.
The inspected Chinese statement includes AB>AC, omitted in the AoPS transcription. It also describes P,Q as a diameter through I; the full Chinese condition is retained.

The compilation prints |a_i|-|a_{i+1}|<=1, whereas AoPS prints |a_i-a_{i+1}|<=1. The latter version is retained: the former would allow arbitrarily large alternating terms and invalidate the finite maximum task.

Domain variant: AoPS asks for positive integers a; the inspected Chinese compilation asks for all integers a. The bank retains the positive-integer AoPS version. The condition depends only on a modulo 37.
The Chinese compilation mislabels the white matching using m instead of n. The white matching has n pairs, as required by its 2n white vertices and confirmed by the AoPS paper.
The AoPS public transcription mistakenly lists x_1,...,x_n before a product of 2023 factors. The inspected Chinese paper confirms exactly 2023 positive integer factors.
The bank retains the exact maximum-cardinality question in the inspected Chinese paper; the AoPS reproduction additionally requests equality cases for its stated bound.
The public AoPS transcription omits that x_1 is a positive integer. This condition is explicit in the inspected Chinese paper reproduction and is restored.

The inspected SM International Education paper reproduction confirms n>=4 and the n^(-3/2) improvement, matching AoPS. A separate Beijing information-site transcription has a garbled formula and n>=3 and was not used for this problem.
